subject.title: [Bug]:  Session status blind spot | Sessions in done state excluded from context saturation monitoring — agents run dead for hours undetected

question: Should saturated terminal `done` sessions become a native OpenClaw diagnostic or health alert, and what threshold, target, and recovery action should that alert use?
rationale: Current code exposes context data but has no documented or tested contract for treating terminal context pressure as an alertable condition; adding one affects operator notifications, diagnostics semantics, and possibly config/recovery behavior.

options.title: Define native context-pressure diagnostics
options.body: Add an explicit session context-pressure classification or health warning for active and terminal saturated rows, preferring existing context-budget data before adding new config.

options.title: Keep this observe-only for now
options.body: Leave context saturation visible through status/telemetry surfaces and document that custom fleet monitoring remains the operator path until live proof and semantics are clearer.

options.title: Defer to broader context work
options.body: Wait for the context-pressure telemetry or continuation work to land, then re-evaluate whether a narrower terminal-session alert is still needed.

recommendation.title: Define native context-pressure diagnostics
recommendation.body: Add an explicit session context-pressure classification or health warning for active and terminal saturated rows, preferring existing context-budget data before adding new config.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest current routing candidate for diagnostics/session-attention behavior based on current source blame and recent diagnostics work.
